mobile-bff error rate metric spiked starting at 2026-10-13T13:41:00+00:00, reaching 5.36% error rate.
notification-service showed no error rate or latency anomaly during the incident window.
auth-service logs show frequent 503 Service Unavailable errors from otp-provider beginning at 2026-10-13T13:40:13+00:00.
auth-service users hit OTP resend limits starting at 2026-10-13T13:42:35+00:00 due to upstream delivery failures.

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependency graphs for auth-service, mobile-bff, notification-service, and sms-vendor, and gathered all deployments, configuration changes, and feature flags across the system over the last 7 days. Identified key changes including auth-service deploy chg-9363 at 13:05 on 2026-10-13.

findings.statement: auth-service depends synchronously on user-db, redis-session, and otp-provider.
mobile-bff depends synchronously on auth-service, payments-api, portfolio-service, orders-service, kyc-service, and aa-connector.
notification-service depends asynchronously on event-bus and synchronously on sms-vendor and push-provider.
auth-service was deployed at 2026-10-13T13:05:00+00:00 (chg-9363) with summary 'auth-service v7.1.3: limit OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes'.
orders-service was deployed at 2026-10-13T12:24:00+00:00 (chg-8588) prior to the incident.
ledger-db was deployed at 2026-10-13T12:34:00+00:00 (chg-9012) prior to the incident.

open_questions: Did the OTP limit change in chg-9363 contribute to the user-reported failures, or are they coming from downstream otp-provider issues?

r2-observability-1.summary: External otp-provider experienced a severe degradation starting precisely at 13:40 UTC on 2026-10-13, characterized by an error rate spike up to 80.04% and p99 latency jumping to ~5.5s, which directly explains the 503 errors and OTP delivery failures observed in auth-service and mobile-bff.

findings.statement: otp-provider error rate spiked starting at 13:40 UTC, reaching a peak of 80.04% at 13:52 UTC.
otp-provider p99 latency increased starting at 13:40 UTC, reaching a peak of 5495.16 ms at 13:56 UTC.
otp-provider request rate (rps) remained normal without any anomaly during the incident window.
auth-service began logging 503 Service Unavailable errors from otp-provider starting at 13:40 UTC.
mobile-bff experienced a concurrent error rate increase starting at 13:41 UTC.

open_questions: What specific internal failure or infrastructure outage occurred at the external otp-provider service at 13:40 UTC?

hypotheses.title: Third-Party OTP Provider Outage
hypotheses.mechanism: The external third-party otp-provider experienced a severe degradation and outage starting at 13:40 UTC, evidenced by a sharp increase in its error rate up to 80.04% and p99 latency jumping to ~5.5s, which caused dependent auth-service calls to fail with 503 Service Unavailable responses and mobile-bff to experience error rate spikes.

supporting.note: otp-provider error rate spiked starting at 13:40 UTC, reaching a peak of 80.04%.
otp-provider p99 latency increased starting at 13:40 UTC, peaking at ~5.5s.
Shows auth-service receiving 503 Service Unavailable errors from otp-provider starting at 13:40.
Auth-service error rate sharply spiked starting at 13:40.
Mobile-bff error rate spiked immediately after at 13:41 due to dependency on auth-service.

assumptions: The root cause of otp-provider's degradation is internal to the third-party vendor's infrastructure, as request rates (rps) remained normal.

hypotheses.title: Auth-Service Deployment Regression
hypotheses.mechanism: Deploying chg-9363 (limiting OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes) at 13:05 introduced a bug or improper request handling that triggered upstream 503 errors from otp-provider.

supporting.note: A deployment occurred on auth-service shortly before the incident window at 13:05.
Users hit OTP resend limits starting at 13:42, which relates directly to the feature introduced in chg-9363.

contradicting.note: otp-provider error rate spiked independently at 13:40, indicating provider-side failure rather than a client-triggered issue.
otp-provider latency degraded significantly starting at 13:40.
Explicit 503 Service Unavailable responses indicate server-side vendor unavailability.

assumptions: A client-side change in auth-service could cause a third-party vendor service to throw server-side 503 Service Unavailable errors while request rates remain completely stable.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The Critic pointed out that H1 lacked direct metrics or logs from otp-provider itself. In response, r2-observability-1 retrieved telemetry directly for otp-provider, confirming that its error rate spiked up to 80.04% and p99 latency increased to ~5.5s starting precisely at 13:40 UTC. This completely validates H1, turning it from an unverified assumption into a robust, fact-backed conclusion. H2 remains an extremely weak alternative since explicit 503 errors and direct provider-side degradation metrics conclusively point to an external vendor outage.
